transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ChatGPT. What brings you in today?

Well, Doctor, I’m here because... well, honestly, it’s been going on for months now, and I just can't get anyone to listen to me. I’ve been keeping track, you know, really paying attention to the details, because as an administrative supervisor, I know when things aren't adding up. And I’ve been seeing this same pattern over and over again. It started with my sister’s medical appointments—they just kept getting moved or rescheduled without anyone telling me, and then the bills started showing up wrong, with strange charges or sent to the wrong address. And the phone calls! People constantly "forgetting" to call me back, or saying they left a message when I know for a fact my phone never rang. I've checked the call logs. I know how systems work. And even when everyone—my family, the receptionists, everyone—keeps telling me, "Oh, it’s just a clerical error," or "Oh, it's just a mistake," I know better. I know they’re deliberately keeping information from me. They are actively trying to push me out of making decisions for my sister, and they're coordinating it, I just know it. It's not just a coincidence when it happens this many times, in this specific way.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people do not?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I'm not imagining things, if that's what you're getting at. My vision and hearing are absolutely fine. Actually, I just went to the optometrist back in... I want to say late October? Yes, October, because it was right before the end-of-year audit at work, and I needed to make sure my reading glasses prescription was up to date for all the spreadsheets I have to review. My eyes are perfectly fine. And my hearing is sharp—you have to have good ears when you're managing an office of twenty people, believe me. You hear every little whisper. 

So, no, I'm not hearing voices or seeing ghosts or whatever it is people see. Everything I am talking about is real, physical evidence. I'm talking about tangible things. Like, I will literally be holding a piece of paper—a printed medical bill with the wrong billing codes and a completely different address on it—and I'll show it to my family or the clinic manager, and they'll just brush it off. Or I'll have my cell phone in my hand, looking at the exact carrier logs I downloaded as a PDF, proving that no call ever came through to my device at 2:15 PM on a Tuesday like they claimed. It's all right there in black and white. I have files of it. 

So it's not that I'm seeing things that aren't there, Doctor. It's that everyone else is deliberately pretending *not* to see the things that *are* there, just to make me look like I don't know what I'm talking about.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in things?

No, no, I haven't been depressed. I mean, frustrated? Yes. Exhausted? Absolutely. But not depressed in the way you mean. I haven't lost interest in anything. In fact, it’s quite the opposite. I am highly motivated, highly engaged. I have to be, don't I? If I lose focus for even a day, they’ll slip something past me. Just last weekend, my husband asked if I wanted to go to the botanical gardens—we used to go a lot in the spring, it's lovely, they have these incredible rhododendrons—but I told him I couldn't, because I had to spend the afternoon cross-referencing the latest batch of Explanation of Benefits statements with the appointment calendar. I mean, it took me four hours just to organize the paperwork from April alone. 

So it's not a lack of interest, Doctor. I am very interested in getting to the bottom of this. I still enjoy my work, I still manage my team effectively—though I will admit, I've had to be a bit more vigilant at the office lately, making sure my own files aren't being tampered with while I'm dealing with all this personal stress. But depressed? Lying in bed all day, not caring about anything? No. I don't have the luxury of not caring. If I don't stay on top of this, who will? They're banking on me getting tired and just giving up, but I won't. I simply won't.
Have you ever had any other times in your life when you held similar beliefs like this, even when your mood was otherwise normal?

No, nothing like this. I mean, why would I? This isn't just some... some phase or something I make up in my head. I've never had to deal with anything like this before because, well, people haven't been actively trying to sabotage me before! 

I've always been very level-headed. You don't get to be an administrative supervisor by jumping at shadows. I started at my company twenty-two years ago—twenty-two years this coming August, actually. I worked my way up from a basic data entry clerk, and you don't do that if you're the sort of person who just imagines conspiracies everywhere. I've always been the one people rely on to keep things organized, to make sure the filing system is impeccable, to ensure the quarterly reports are flawless. I've always had a very clear view of reality. 

Sure, there have been office politics over the years—there was this one time back in 2015 when a junior associate tried to take credit for a workflow restructuring I designed, but that was just typical corporate ladder-climbing. I handled it professionally, I documented everything, and HR took care of it. But that was just one person being ambitious. It wasn't this... this coordinated effort. It wasn't people messing with my sister's medical records or lying to my face about phone calls. 

So, no, Doctor. I've never had "beliefs" like this before, because this isn't a belief. It's happening right now. It's unprecedented. And honestly, it's exhausting that I have to keep defending myself like this when I'm the one being targeted. I just want someone to look at the evidence I've collected instead of asking me if I've always been like this. I haven't. I'm just trying to deal with what's happening to me right now.
Have you noticed your thoughts being put into your head, taken away, or broadcast so other people can hear them?

No, no, that's... no. That sounds like science fiction, Doctor. My thoughts are my own. Nobody is putting them there, and nobody is taking them away. And broadcast? Like on a radio frequency? No, of course not. I mean, if they could hear my thoughts, they wouldn't need to go to all the trouble of tampering with my files and lying about phone records, would they? They'd just know what I was planning to do next. 

But really, how would that even work? The human brain is a closed system. I remember reading an article about this—well, not this exactly, but about neural pathways and how complex the brain is—back when my mother was dealing with some mild cognitive decline. It was in one of those science magazines my husband subscribes to, the ones with the glossy covers. Anyway, the point is, nobody can just reach into your head and pull out a thought. That's ridiculous. 

My problem isn't that people can hear what I'm thinking. My problem is that people aren't listening to what I'm *saying*. I will literally stand there and explain to them, step by step, how the billing codes on the statements don't match the standard coding manual—which I know very well, by the way, because I have to cross-reference codes for our departmental budget all the time—and they just look at me like I'm speaking a foreign language. They don't need telepathy to know what I'm thinking because I am telling them directly! I am laying it all out for them, plain as day, with documentation to back it up, and they just... they dismiss it. So no, my thoughts are perfectly safe inside my own head. It's the physical evidence out here in the real world that keeps getting messed with.
